correctness.rationale: The exact source-row criterion follows by considering each nontrivial lower-to-upper order comparison and whether the accessibility target is maximal or minimal. The two disjoint cases Z=empty and |Z|=z>=1 enumerate all upper-source rows, with Q-membership weights computed independently per lower target. The relaxed L(a,b) count factorizes into b upper-target columns; the weighted event of an empty upper-source row is at most b(2^(b-1)/H)^b. Exact integer exhaustive checks for all relations on six small labelled posets and independent upper-row sums in five further cases corroborate the derivation. The uniform asymptotic follows from an actual finite relative-error inequality, not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: Complete bipartite height-two posets are the first naturally symmetric intuitionistic orders with arbitrary branching at both levels. Forward confluence is the central semantic constraint for a recently investigated modal system. The two-parameter count F(a,b) is a natural exact finite-frame invariant, not an arbitrary numerical slice; it also yields an all-a uniform asymptotic and two distinct exponential regimes of random-frame rarity. The a=1 specialization was already known, whereas the common-intersection coupling between multiple lower and upper sources is new in the comparison set. This supplies a baseline for sampling finite FIK frames and for comparison with stronger confluence axioms.
